1	---
2	title: Many-to-many relations
3	description: How to define and work with many-to-many relations in Prisma.
4	url: /orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/many-to-many-relations
5	metaDescription: How to define and work with many-to-many relations in Prisma.
6	metaTitle: Many-to-many relations
7	---
8	
9	Many-to-many (m-n) relations connect zero or more records on one side to zero or more on the other. They can be [implicit](#implicit-many-to-many-relations) (Prisma manages the relation table) or [explicit](#explicit-many-to-many-relations) (you define the relation table).
10	
11	## Relational databases
12	
13	Use [implicit](#implicit-many-to-many-relations) m-n unless you need to store additional metadata in the relation table.
14	
15	### Explicit many-to-many relations
16	
17	The relation table is represented as a model in the schema:
18	
19	```prisma
20	model Post {
21	  id         Int                 @id @default(autoincrement())
22	  title      String
23	  categories CategoriesOnPosts[]
24	}
25	
26	model Category {
27	  id    Int                 @id @default(autoincrement())
28	  name  String
29	  posts CategoriesOnPosts[]
30	}
31	
32	model CategoriesOnPosts {
33	  post       Post     @relation(fields: [postId], references: [id])
34	  postId     Int
35	  category   Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id])
36	  categoryId Int
37	  assignedAt DateTime @default(now())
38	  assignedBy String
39	  @@id([postId, categoryId])
40	}
41	```
42	
43	The relation table can store additional fields like `assignedAt` and `assignedBy`.
44	
45	#### Querying explicit many-to-many
46	
47	```ts
48	// Create post with new category
49	const post = await prisma.post.create({
50	  data: {
51	    title: "How to be Bob",
52	    categories: {
53	      create: [
54	        {
55	          assignedBy: "Bob",
56	          category: { create: { name: "New category" } },
57	        },
58	      ],
59	    },
60	  },
61	});
62	
63	// Connect to existing categories
64	await prisma.post.create({
65	  data: {
66	    title: "My Post",
67	    categories: {
68	      create: [
69	        { assignedBy: "Bob", category: { connect: { id: 9 } } },
70	        { assignedBy: "Bob", category: { connect: { id: 22 } } },
71	      ],
72	    },
73	  },
74	});
75	
76	// Query posts by category
77	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
78	  where: { categories: { some: { category: { name: "New Category" } } } },
79	});
80	```
81	
82	### Implicit many-to-many relations
83	
84	Prisma manages the relation table automatically:
85	
86	```prisma
87	model Post {
88	  id         Int        @id @default(autoincrement())
89	  title      String
90	  categories Category[]
91	}
92	
93	model Category {
94	  id    Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
95	  name  String
96	  posts Post[]
97	}
98	```
99	
100	#### Querying implicit many-to-many
101	
102	```ts
103	// Create post with categories
104	const post = await prisma.post.create({
105	  data: {
106	    title: "How to become a butterfly",
107	    categories: {
108	      create: [{ name: "Magic" }, { name: "Butterflies" }],
109	    },
110	  },
111	});
112	
113	// Get posts with categories
114	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
115	  include: { categories: true },
116	});
117	```
118	
119	#### Rules for implicit m-n
120	
121	- Both models must have a single `@id` (no composite IDs or `@unique`)
122	- No `@relation` attribute needed (unless disambiguating)
123	- Cannot use `fields`, `references`, `onUpdate`, or `onDelete` in `@relation`
124	
125	#### Relation table conventions
126	
127	For `prisma db pull` to recognize implicit m-n tables:
128	
129	- Table name: `_CategoryToPost` (underscore + model names alphabetically + `To`)
130	- Columns: `A` (FK to first model alphabetically) and `B` (FK to second)
131	- Unique index on both columns, non-unique index on `B`
132	
133	### Configuring relation table name
134	
135	Use `@relation("MyRelationTable")` on both sides to customize the table name.
136	
137	## MongoDB
138	
139	MongoDB requires explicit ID arrays on both sides:
140	
141	```prisma
142	model Post {
143	  id          String     @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId
144	  categoryIDs String[]   @db.ObjectId
145	  categories  Category[] @relation(fields: [categoryIDs], references: [id])
146	}
147	
148	model Category {
149	  id      String   @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId
150	  name    String
151	  postIDs String[] @db.ObjectId
152	  posts   Post[]   @relation(fields: [postIDs], references: [id])
153	}
154	```
155	
156	### Querying MongoDB m-n
157	
158	```ts
159	// Find posts by category IDs
160	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
161	  where: { categoryIDs: { hasSome: [id1, id2] } },
162	});
163	
164	// Find posts by category name
165	const posts = await prisma.post.findMany({
166	  where: { categories: { some: { name: { contains: "Servers" } } } },
167	});
168	```
